ov.idea: Introducono la 'Gumbel substitution': il coordinatore fissa un rumore Gumbel pubblico per ogni posizione di token, identico bit per bit su tutte le GPU, e il sampler estrae y = argmax(ℓ^q + G). Il trainer ricalcola v* = argmax(ℓ^p + G), il token che la sua policy avrebbe estratto con lo stesso rumore, e assegna un punteggio a v* nel contesto del sampler. Per un sampler che segue il protocollo, v* è un campione esatto da p dato il prefisso, quindi la deriva svanisce in aspettativa per qualsiasi q, senza probabilità riportate dal sampler.
ov.risultati: In laboratorio, su un modello 9B con la stessa testa su entrambi i lati, la deriva attesa dell'addestramento non corretto è almeno 170–4.800 volte quella della sostituzione. Su un modello 2B con forte disallineamento, l'addestramento non corretto collassa mentre la sostituzione resta stabile, comparabile a MIS con score centering dato il vero q.
ov.limiti: Il testo è troncato e non riporta i risultati completi sul network permissionless con modello 9B.

glossario.d: Componente che genera i rollout campionando token dalla policy.
Rumore casuale usato per campionare da una distribuzione tramite argmax.
Deriva: scostamento sistematico della distribuzione di addestramento da quella desiderata.

2611.27032.abs: As large reasoning models (LRMs) become more capable, reliable evaluation becomes essential. LRMs can sometimes recognize that they are being evaluated, a phenomenon known as \emph{evaluation awareness}. This phenomenon raises concerns about whether safety behavior, particularly refusal behavior, generalizes from evaluation to deployment. Prior work manipulates \emph{verbalized evaluation awareness (VEA)} through activation steering and observes higher refusal rates when VEA is present, but the mechanisms underlying this connection remain poorly understood. We identify \emph{VEA neurons} by contrasting their activations in VEA and non-VEA reasoning segments. Intervening on 5,000 VEA neurons reduces the VEA rate from 12.6--51.8\% to at most 1.4\% across the model benchmark combinations in our main experiments, and lowers a probe score for unverbalized evaluation awareness (unVEA). In QwQ-32B, VEA-neuron intervention also reduces refusal even in rollouts without VEA; VEA text itself explains only 4--10\% of the decrease. We further show that their down-projection vectors contain refusal components, and preserving these components during intervention partially restores refusal while maintaining VEA suppression, accounting for about half of the refusal decrease and providing a mechanistic explanation for the connection between evaluation awareness and refusal. Finally, across the OLMo 3 SFT, DPO, and RLVR checkpoints, the VEA rate on SorryBench and StrongREJECT is similar after SFT and DPO but substantially higher after RLVR, alongside an increase in the number of VEA neurons.…

ov.problema: I grandi modelli di ragionamento a volte capiscono di essere in fase di valutazione (evaluation awareness) e questo può far aumentare i rifiuti a rispondere; non era chiaro il meccanismo che collega i due fenomeni.
ov.idea: Gli autori individuano i 'neuroni VEA' confrontando le loro attivazioni nei segmenti di ragionamento con e senza evaluation awareness verbalizzata. Intervenendo su 5.000 di questi neuroni riducono la VEA e mostrano che i loro vettori di down-projection contengono componenti legate al rifiuto: preservandole durante l'intervento il rifiuto torna in parte.
ov.risultati: L'intervento sui neuroni VEA riduce il tasso di VEA dal 12,6–51,8% a non più dell'1,4% nelle combinazioni modello-benchmark testate e abbassa un probe per la evaluation awareness non verbalizzata. In QwQ-32B riduce anche il rifiuto in rollout senza VEA, ma il testo VEA spiega solo il 4–10% della diminuzione; preservare le componenti di rifiuto recupera circa metà della riduzione del rifiuto.
ov.limiti: Il testo è troncato e non riporta i risultati finali sui checkpoint OLMo 3 SFT, DPO e RLVR.

glossario.d: Evaluation awareness verbalizzata: il modello dice esplicitamente di essere valutato.
Modificare le attivazioni interne durante l'inferenza per cambiare il comportamento.
Matrice che proietta l'attivazione di un neurone verso lo spazio di output.

2611.26855.abs: Flow matching policies underpin the state-of-the-art in robot learning, with impressive results ranging from long-horizon planning to dexterous manipulation. However, they provide no measure of whether their predicted commands can be trusted, particularly in novel situations outside their training set. Epistemic uncertainty reflects uncertainty about the model's weights and quantifies this ignorance, but calculating it at inference time from a flow matching policy is not trivial. Actions are produced by an ODE solver, requiring uncertainty to be propagated through the entire integration process. BayesDiff addresses this problem for diffusion models by propagating the mean and variance of the state through the denoising chain under a last-layer Laplace posterior approximation, but it severely underestimates the epistemic uncertainty. In this paper we: i) prove that, for flow matching and diffusion ODEs, BayesDiff's total variance decays at rate $O(1/T)$ as the number of Euler steps $T$ used by the solver increases; ii) introduce Coherent Moment Propagation (CoMP), two recursions inspired by the extended and unscented Kalman filters that fix this problem by carrying the cross-covariance between state and weights; and iii) widen the last-layer posterior with observation embeddings the policy already computes, improving uncertainty estimates without retraining for CoMP and several test-time estimators alike. We demonstrate these benefits on three manipulation benchmarks with applications in failure detection and demonstration selection for fine-tuning, where CoMP corrects…

2611.27094.abs: LLM agents are being proposed for bank model validation, yet evaluations that compare agent-assisted work with manual practice credit the agent with gains that come from digitized evidence and deterministic tests. We propose a staged architecture in which an LLM-free controlled workflow (P1) is both the fallback and the control arm for individually authorized agent tasks (P2), and an attribution protocol that credits an agent only for faults P1 does not already report. The protocol charges decoy false alarms, unnecessary actions and endorsed developer assertions, counts invalid outputs as misses, folds newly automatable findings back into P1 with discovery credit, and fixes safety bounds and a break-even cost gate in advance. On a synthetic credit-scorecard harness, five scripted reference policies show why this matters: naive case accuracy (4/6) and pooled detection (3/5) tie four flawed policies, whereas the protocol separates all five and credits only the reference policy with detection beyond P1. One fold-back round raises a P1-parroting policy's naive scores without any change to the policy. A regression matrix of sixteen mutants covers nine ways in which earlier versions of the evaluation passed misleadingly. No LLM agent has been evaluated yet; we specify a falsifiable pilot.

2611.27187.abs: Single-modality action-expert pretraining controls competition from visual shortcuts before vision--language--action (VLA) adaptation. Yet single-modality pretraining can impair the vision--language interactions needed for subsequent joint prediction. We construct a diagnostic model in which VA or LA pretraining can disable an initially active pathway for joint vision--language modeling. In this model, subsequent training with complete visual and language inputs cannot restore the pathway, even with unlimited adaptation. We therefore introduce Stochastic Context for Action Expert Pretraining (SCAP), a new action-expert pretraining stage that precedes full-input training. During this stage, visual and text tokens are randomly masked before entering the VLM. In this unified diagnostic model, SCAP can preserve the joint vision--language modeling pathway during pretraining and subsequent full-input training. Compared with direct full-input training, it can also reduce reliance on visual shortcuts and increase reliance on language instructions. SCAP consistently improves performance across four different VLA architectures. In real-robot experiments, it achieves 76.67% average success across three instruction-conditioned manipulation tasks, outperforming full-input pretraining by 25 percentage points.

2611.27330.abs: A planner deciding whether to turn left or continue straight needs to inspect different parts of the scene for each maneuver. Yet many end-to-end driving planners evaluate every candidate trajectory against the same compressed scene representation. We let each candidate select the visual evidence used to refine and score it. A global glance first produces trajectory hypotheses from shared scene features. We then project a corridor around each trajectory into the camera views and use the resulting mask to attend to patch features at the backbone's native resolution. After refinement, the scorer projects each final proposal again and ranks it using evidence along its own path. This geometric selection requires only the predicted trajectory and camera calibration. On three planners with different scene representations (learned registers, a perception-supervised bird's-eye-view grid, and a coarse image-token grid), adding this gaze improves planning scores. In ablations, path-aligned patches outperform both a matched number of randomly selected patches and attention over all patches. Using the gaze for ranking yields larger gains than using it for refinement alone. With a ViT-S backbone and no perception labels, GGDriver achieves a rater feedback score of 8.110 on the WOD-E2E test set, 94.2 PDMS on NAVSIM-v1, 48.6 EPDMS on NAVSIM-v2, and a closed-loop Driving Score of 72.18 on Bench2Drive.

2611.26996.abs: How does future prediction affect context-dependent robot control? We introduce PonderPounce-WM, extending PonderPounce with three future tokens supervised to predict visual-feature changes. Its pretrained MLLM, Ponder, integrates history and demonstrations into continuous cognition for the action model, Pounce. We investigate token ordering and delivery to distinguish predictive supervision from direct future conditioning. On RoboMME, cognition-first ordering with cognition-only delivery improves success from 60.83% to 67.42%. With the same ordering, direct future-token delivery yields 64.00% success. Probes show increased future information in cognition while the tested past-event attributes remain largely decodable. Across four real-robot tasks, PonderPounce-WM achieves 67.44% mean success under asynchronous execution, compared with 60.98% for PonderPounce. These results suggest that future prediction can improve context-dependent control through auxiliary supervision without delivering future tokens to the action model.

2611.26797.abs: Generative models now write working code, produce realistic images, and hold long conversations, yet the mechanisms behind their intelligence still evade our understanding. This thesis explores that puzzle through Associative Memory (AM), in which patterns are stored as energy minima and retrieved through attractor dynamics. Beyond their capacity, AMs form new minima known as spurious states, long regarded as a failure of memory. We argue that this failure is where creativity begins, and that memorization and generalization can coexist as outcomes of one retrieval process. First, we show that diffusion models behave as AMs. With little data, a diffusion model forms a distinct basin of attraction around each training sample. As the data grows, these basins shrink, and spurious states emerge as attractors that blend stored samples yet match none of them. They are the first signs of generative capability. We characterize this transition by measuring the volume, energy, and curvature of these basins across datasets and architectures, including Stable Diffusion. We then turn to language and move beyond the energy-based view of AM. We show that uniform-state discrete diffusion models are AMs capable of retrieving unseen data, with basins of attraction that arise from conditional likelihood maximization alone. As the training set grows, basins around training examples contract while basins around unseen examples expand, until corrupted test sentences are recovered as reliably as training ones. Conditional entropy exposes this coexistence within a single sequence and cheaply…

ov.problema: I modelli generativi producono risultati impressionanti, ma i meccanismi alla base della loro intelligenza non sono chiari. In particolare, non si capisce come memorizzazione e generalizzazione coesistano.
ov.idea: La tesi esplora questo problema attraverso la memoria associativa (AM), dove i pattern sono immagazzinati come minimi di energia e recuperati tramite dinamiche attrattive. Gli autori mostrano che i modelli di diffusione si comportano come AM: con pochi dati formano bacini di attrazione attorno a ogni esempio di training; con più dati, questi bacini si restringono e emergono stati spuri (minimi che mescolano esempi memorizzati ma non corrispondono a nessuno), che sono i primi segni di capacità generativa. Lo stesso vale per modelli di diffusione discreta uniforme nel linguaggio.
ov.risultati: Vengono caratterizzati volume, energia e curvatura dei bacini in vari dataset e architetture, inclusa Stable Diffusion. Nei modelli di diffusione discreta, i bacini attorno agli esempi di training si contraggono mentre quelli attorno a esempi non visti si espandono, fino a recuperare frasi corrotte in modo affidabile.

glossario.d: Modello che immagazzina pattern come minimi di energia e li recupera.
Minimi di energia che non corrispondono a pattern memorizzati.
Modello generativo che impara a denoising dati rumorosi.

2611.27090.abs: When an AI coding agent deletes the wrong files or a long agent run crashes, users fall back on recovery mechanisms: resume from a checkpoint, undo, ask for approval, read the log. Research runtimes promise stronger guarantees, such as saga-style compensation and transactional rollback. We ask what public evidence shows about whether either kind works in real use. Under a protocol frozen before data collection, we graded 12 persistent agent runtimes, 26 coding-agent harnesses and 12 research runtimes on eight recovery mechanisms, from not found to exercised in a real run, with two blind coding passes, adjudication and re-verification against archived sources. Recovery is exercised almost everywhere in practice: 11 of 12 runtimes and 25 of 26 harnesses have at least one real-use report. Yet of 128 such reports, only 19 describe the run fully recovering; 54 are partial and 45 failed. Checkpoint/resume recovered once in 27 reports, rollback once in 15. Research runtimes show the opposite profile: guarantees evaluated on benchmarks, none reported in operation, and compensation of external effects, their central guarantee, is offered by no harness at all.

2611.27158.abs: Foundation models have advanced SAR image interpretation but created a heterogeneous, fragmented model ecosystem. Existing models differ substantially in their input, training data, objectives, architectures, and release policy, yet the field lacks a unified taxonomy and comparative framework. Current evaluations rely primarily on task-specific benchmarks, which are ill-suited to fair comparison among models with fundamentally different input-output formats and task paradigms, and often overlook data transparency, reproducibility, interpretability, and deployment readiness. Limited SAR data accessibility also means high reported performance does not guarantee access to training data, code, or weights, limiting reproduction, benchmarking, and deployment. To address these issues, we propose a systematic taxonomy and hierarchical evaluation framework for SAR-related foundation models: five rating levels, six dimensions, and fine-grained criteria, with separate protocols for VFMs and VLMs. Beyond overall ratings, it yields interpretable multidimensional capability profiles and supports user-defined weighting, so rankings follow user priorities. Utilizing a fixed auxiliary multimodal large language model in combination with human review, we conduct a systematic meta-analysis and multidimensional assessment of 76 VFMs and 40 VLMs. In terms of SAR benchmark task performance under our framework, SAR-native VLMs do not significantly outperform remote sensing VLMs pretrained on mixed multimodal corpora in which SAR is one of several modalities. This lack of clear advantage is…

2611.26975.abs: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. On Qwen3-0.6B, ToRA matches or beats a dedicated streaming guard, with higher F1 on 12 of 17 benchmarks. It detects 11.8 points more unsafe responses than the probe at a similar cost, under 4% added latency per token.

ov.problema: Quando un LLM locale serve un solo utente, il decoding è limitato dalla banda di memoria e la potenza di calcolo resta inutilizzata. I controlli di sicurezza in streaming oggi costano troppo: un modello guardiano dedicato raddoppia la latenza per token, mentre una sonda sugli stati nascosti è economica ma meno accurata.
ov.idea: ToRA è un adattatore che fa girare un secondo modello come una riga extra nel passo di decoding del generatore, condividendo pesi e KV cache. I kernel 'dual-row' leggono ogni peso una sola volta per entrambe le righe, così il controllo di sicurezza quasi non aggiunge costo.
ov.risultati: Su Qwen3-0.6B, ToRA eguaglia o batte un guardiano in streaming dedicato, con F1 più alto su 12 benchmark su 17. Rileva l'11,8% in più di risposte non sicure rispetto alla sonda a costo simile, con meno del 4% di latenza aggiuntiva per token.
ov.limiti: I risultati sono misurati solo su Qwen3-0.6B; non è chiaro se il guadagno si mantenga su modelli più grandi.

2611.27070.abs: Recent studies have shown that visual tools can improve multimodal reasoning. However, the effects of tools vary substantially across samples, and benchmark accuracy alone does not reveal whether tool interactions are beneficial or redundant. We present $R^2$, a framework that recognizes and reduces redundant visual tool use in vision-language models. We first introduce a sample-level Category Analysis of Tool Utility (CAT), which categorizes samples according to whether a model can benefit from tools. This analysis reveals that benchmark scores may obscure a model's tool-use ability. Across seven benchmarks, samples benefiting from tools account for at most 12.44% of each benchmark, while the majority gain little from tool interaction or are even harmed by it. To assess individual calls, we propose the Visual Feedback Dependency (VFD) metric, which compares the likelihood of the same subsequent reasoning under actual and alternative visual feedback without an external evaluator or trajectory regeneration. Redundancy-Aware GRPO (RA-GRPO) combines this dependency signal with a category-conditioned base call cost to assign relative efficiency advantages among correct trajectories, supplementing outcome-based supervision. Across the seven benchmarks, RA-GRPO reduces the mean number of tool calls by 12.39% relative to Vanilla GRPO at comparable benchmark accuracy. Evaluated by tool-utility category, RA-GRPO improves category macro-average accuracy over Vanilla GRPO by 3.35 percentage points.

ov.problema: I modelli visione-linguaggio (VLM) usano strumenti visivi per migliorare il ragionamento, ma non è chiaro se questi strumenti siano sempre utili o a volte ridondanti. La sola accuratezza sui benchmark non rivela se l'interazione con lo strumento è benefica o dannosa.
ov.idea: Gli autori propongono R^2, un framework che riconosce e riduce l'uso ridondante di strumenti visivi. Introducono CAT (Category Analysis of Tool Utility) per categorizzare i campioni in base al beneficio dello strumento, e VFD (Visual Feedback Dependency) per misurare quanto la risposta dipende dal feedback visivo. Poi usano RA-GRPO (Redundancy-Aware GRPO) che combina VFD con un costo base per chiamata, per assegnare vantaggi di efficienza tra traiettorie corrette.
ov.risultati: Su sette benchmark, i campioni che beneficiano degli strumenti sono al massimo il 12.44%. RA-GRPO riduce il numero medio di chiamate agli strumenti del 12.39% rispetto a Vanilla GRPO, con accuratezza comparabile, e migliora l'accuratezza macro-media per categoria del 3.35%.

glossario.d: Modello che elabora sia immagini che testo.
Metodo di ottimizzazione per modelli linguistici basato su ricompense.
Insieme di test standardizzati per valutare le prestazioni.

2611.27128.abs: In this paper, we analyze multi-layer visual representations in large vision-language models (LVLMs) and examine the effectiveness of layer-wise features and multi-layer fusion for anomaly detection. Representative LVLMs connect visual encoder features to a language model through a projector. In this design, deep visual encoder features carry high-level semantics and alignment with text representations, whereas shallow and intermediate layers retain information relevant to vision-centric tasks, such as local appearance and fine-grained shape. It is therefore important to choose layer representations and fusion methods according to the nature of the downstream task. Focusing on anomaly detection, we compare layer-wise features and multi-layer fusion across multiple supervision levels and a variety of classifiers, and examine from several perspectives how multi-layer visual representations affect downstream performance. By analyzing the resulting performance differences, we further discuss the contribution of each layer representation to anomaly detection and provide empirical insights into representation selection for vision-centric tasks.

2611.26949.abs: Human visual perception is dynamically shaped by the recent past, a phenomenon known as serial dependence. Mechanistic models show that a residual memory trace can generate this dependency, yet its functional purpose (why the visual system should carry information forward in time at all) remains debated. We tested the hypothesis that serial dependence emerges as a normative consequence of optimizing vision for robustness against sensory noise. We trained recurrent autoencoders (a CNN encoder, a ConvGRU memory module, and a CNN decoder) to reconstruct natural videos corrupted by Gaussian noise, with no objective referring to perceptual history. Models that used their temporal memory achieved lower reconstruction error than memory-free counterparts, and this advantage widened as training noise increased, indicating that integrating past context is an adaptive denoising strategy. Probing the trained models with Gabor and dot sequences, we found that memory gave rise to serial dependence spontaneously: an attractive bias toward previous orientations and a spatial "continuity field" toward recently seen locations, both strengthening with training noise. Across temporal delays, the model's serial dependence was strongest for the immediately preceding stimulus and decayed monotonically. This profile quantitatively matched human orientation judgments, including an independent public dataset, once a known response-autocorrelation confound was controlled: an apparent non-monotonicity in one dataset reflected this measurement artifact rather than a genuine model-human mismatch. These…

2611.26988.abs: In letter-of-credit (LC) document examination, a correct final decision does not show that every requirement was examined. We therefore evaluate examination requirement by requirement and make each requirement executable. A language model converts the bill of lading (BL) and commercial invoice (IV) requirements of a credit into atomic conditions and logical structures, and a deterministic verifier retrieves the named evidence and computes each outcome, so every check can be compared with a gold encoding and traced to logged evidence. Because LC records are confidential, our on-premises 9B parser is fine-tuned only on synthetic pairs built from templates and human-reviewed public document values. On 345 real LC cases, final-decision accuracy proves misleading: a constant PASS rule has the highest raw accuracy while examining nothing. Although it never sees a real record during training, the fine-tuned parser detects 93% of the atomic requirements its ontology covers and reconstructs 86% of the covered requirements exactly. It verifies 82% of the evaluable requirements correctly, against 54% for a tool-using agent, and leads the agent on both satisfied requirements and discrepancies. It also completely examines 1.8 times as many cases as few-shot prompting of the same model, while direct prediction and the agent complete none. Executing the gold encodings with the same verifier shows that some of the remaining errors, missed discrepancies included, come from the operators and normalization, which a better parser alone cannot fix. Every rejection comes with a trace of the…

2611.27064.abs: Vision-language models (VLMs) represent each image with hundreds of visual tokens, which can make inference costly even when a prompt depends on only part of the image. Dynamic Token Merging (DTM), introduced in MrT5 for byte-level text encoders, learns which tokens to remove: a lightweight delete gate scores contextualized hidden states, acts as a differentiable attention bias during training, and physically removes tokens at inference. We argue that DTM is a general token deletion framework rather than a byte-level technique, and extend it to the vision modality and to decoder-only models. Applying DTM to T5Gemma 2 and Gemma 3 yields V-MrT5Gemma2, which deletes visual tokens inside a bidirectional multimodal encoder, and V-MrGemma3, which compacts the prompt and its key-value caches during decoder-only prefill. Across ten benchmarks, DTM's advantage over attention-based and random deletion grows with the deletion rate and is largest on document, chart, and scene-text reading. At 80% visual token deletion (approximately 60% fewer FLOPs), DTM raises accuracy over FastV from 51.8 to 63.0 on ChartQA and from 63.3 to 67.8 on TextVQA with V-MrT5Gemma2, as well as from 62.2 to 68.8 and from 71.2 to 75.1 with V-MrGemma3, retaining 90-96% of unpruned performance on both tasks with significant efficiency gains. These results support DTM as a general framework for efficient transformers.

ov.problema: I modelli visione-linguaggio rappresentano ogni immagine con centinaia di token visivi, rendendo l'inferenza costosa anche quando il prompt usa solo una parte dell'immagine.
ov.idea: Dynamic Token Merging (DTM) impara quali token eliminare: un 'delete gate' leggero assegna un punteggio agli stati nascosti, funge da bias di attenzione differenziabile in training e rimuove fisicamente i token a inferenza. Gli autori estendono DTM dalla modalità testo a quella visiva e ai modelli decoder-only.
ov.risultati: Su dieci benchmark il vantaggio di DTM su cancellazione basata su attenzione e casuale cresce col tasso di cancellazione, massimo su documenti, grafici e testo in scena. All'80% di token visivi cancellati (circa 60% di FLOP in meno), DTM porta l'accuratezza su ChartQA da 51,8 a 63,0 e su TextVQA da 63,3 a 67,8 con V-MrT5Gemma2; da 62,2 a 68,8 e da 71,2 a 75,1 con V-MrGemma3, mantenendo il 90-96% delle prestazioni non potate.
ov.limiti: Il testo non chiarisce se il metodo richieda training aggiuntivo per ogni nuovo modello o dominio.

2611.26929.abs: Dani and Liebe (2026) (DL) report that adapting the final encoder block of BIOT and CBraMod with self-supervised learning (SSL) improves CHB-MIT seizure-detection ROC-AUC by 36.2 and 29.5 points over linear probing. We investigate these results with their released code and an independent pipeline. The release loads pretrained weights for adaptation only when an otherwise unset configuration key is supplied, and its CBraMod probe reads the reconstruction head with dropout active. With pretrained initialisation and a probe on the encoder output in evaluation mode, the fixed-recipe adaptation gain on DL's split is -0.6 points for BIOT (95% interval [-3.8, +2.6]) and +0.01 for CBraMod ([-0.02, +0.04]) across five seeds. Across DL's split and five subject rotations on CHB-MIT and Siena Scalp EEG, with equally tuned linear probes (30 configurations, up to 500 epochs, validation-based early stopping), mean adaptation effects range from -1.1 to +5.7 ROC-AUC points over 18 comparisons (related settings and feature variants). Twelve of 18 support equivalence within +/-3 points under dependence-adjusted inference (8 of 12 rotation and 4 of 6 fixed-split comparisons); six are unresolved. After correcting rotation intervals for dependence, no positive effect has a 95% interval excluding zero. The +/-3 margin is an analysis threshold, not a clinically validated one, and smaller margins support fewer equivalences. Two fixed-probe gains near +21 points shrink under the same tuning, with smaller benefits unresolved. We also audit a CHB-MIT protocol shared by at least 14 papers. No tested…

2611.26980.abs: LLM agents such as Hermes, OpenClaw, and Codex repeatedly resend growing execution histories, increasing shared GPU key-value (KV) cache demand in high-bandwidth memory (HBM). We show that shared KV capacity limits agent-serving throughput. Existing context-reduction methods lack global cache-state visibility, while runtime KV managers lack tool-execution information. Tracing tokens to their originating tool operations reveals that later operations supersede earlier outputs and associated turns, identifying 64% of recorded final-history tokens as removal candidates. We present Contexture, a harness- and model-agnostic architecture for runtime context eviction. Contexture separates the harness's full conversation history from the model's execution context, reducing subsequent requests' KV demand without modifying harness logic or model execution. It combines tool-execution information with global visibility into shared KV pressure and prefix residency: supersession identifies removal candidates, while runtime state determines when removal justifies sacrificing cached computation. This coordination reduces memory demand and decode KV traffic while limiting re-prefill interference with concurrent decoding, without additional model calls or training. Across two models, two harnesses, and two benchmarks, Contexture improves throughput under SLO by 20-73% over the best of no eviction, harness compaction, AgentDiet, and Continuum, and by 7-63% over observation masking in five of eight configurations, and reduces GPU energy per completed session by up to 11%. It also raises…

ov.problema: Gli agenti LLM (Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex) rimandano storie di esecuzione sempre più lunghe, aumentando la domanda di KV cache condivisa in HBM. La capacità condivisa limita il throughput del serving agentico.
ov.idea: Tracciando i token fino alle operazioni degli strumenti emerge che le operazioni successive rendono obsolete le precedenti, identificando il 64% dei token finali come candidati alla rimozione. Contexture separa la storia completa dell'harness dal contesto di esecuzione del modello e combina informazioni sugli strumenti con la visibilità globale sulla pressione della KV cache e sulla residenza dei prefissi, decidendo quando rimuovere conviene.
ov.risultati: Su due modelli, due harness e due benchmark, Contexture migliora il throughput sotto SLO del 20-73% rispetto al meglio tra nessuna eviction, compaction dell'harness, AgentDiet e Continuum, e del 7-63% rispetto a observation masking in cinque su sette casi.
ov.limiti: Il testo è troncato e non riporta dettagli su costi di implementazione o su scenari in cui la rimozione possa danneggiare la qualità.

glossario.d: memoria delle chiavi e valori già calcolati, riusata per non ricalcolare i token passati
memoria ad alta banda integrata nelle GPU, dove risiede la KV cache

2611.26913.abs: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides a noninvasive view of functional interactions across the brain, which can be represented as connectivity graphs for neurological disease analysis. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being paired with such representations, yet it remains unclear whether they genuinely reason over the underlying connectivity or simply respond to surface-level cues that may trigger learned priors. We probe this question through a controlled study of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnosis from resting-state functional connectivity, isolating one factor at a time to determine what drives an LLM's predictions on brain connectivity graphs. Across six models, from small open-weight LLMs to a proprietary one, the same pattern holds: the results provide little evidence that predictions are consistently grounded in subject-specific connectivity. Brain region names, numeric formatting, and prompt framing shift what a model predicts without improving how well it separates ADHD subjects from Controls; perturbing the graph changes predictions no more for clinically meaningful regions than for random ones; and the models' own justifications contradict the values they cite, inconsistently interpreting the connectivity evidence provided to them. Across every probe, predictions follow the model's built-in class bias and the surface form of the prompt rather than the subject's connectivity, calling into question a premise underlying current LLM brain integration work. Our code is available at…

2611.26966.abs: Tool-using AI agents propose actions whose authorization and external effects cannot be inferred from generated text alone. We study an execution boundary that separates agent proposals from business-controlled authority, context disclosure, and supplier selection. The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) mediates capability calls and records uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without returning an acceptable reply. We evaluate this runtime with scripted requests and synthetic suppliers: 2,400 fault episodes across four policies, 60 process-termination/restart episodes, 19,000 timed calls across 19 configurations, five targeted mutations over 43 fixtures, and 160 substitution records. No language model or autonomous agent is evaluated. OPCP and a conservative composition agree on all measured fault outcomes. Both recover after definite refusal without cross-supplier duplication; retry-all duplicates effects in every tested lost-reply-after-commit case. Persistent runtime state prevents cross-supplier replay in the restart experiments, while same-supplier duplicate prevention also requires supplier idempotency. At 128 suppliers, best-score routing has a median latency of 1.411 ms versus 0.261 ms for pinned routing. All five selected mutations are detected, and record enumeration exposes acceptance of an empty regression set. These results characterize an execution mechanism relevant to agent governance, including its costs and assumption boundaries. They do not establish improved agent task success, prompt-injection resistance, or real-vendor model portability.

2611.26867.abs: Learning robotic ultrasound policies requires interactive environments for scalable data generation and repeatable evaluation, while exploration on real patients is limited by acquisition costs and safety constraints. Generative world models offer an alternative, but image history and probe actions alone do not ensure anatomical consistency across wide-range scans and changing acoustic windows. We introduce SonoAtlasWorld, an ultrasound world model built on anatomy as state. A persistent 3D anatomical asset extracted from computed tomography (CT) anchors each scan to a specific anatomy. Probe actions determine anatomical and acoustic visibility conditions for a causal ultrasound generator trained on clinical videos. Our three-stage pipeline combines anatomy-conditioned pretraining, causal conversion and long-rollout alignment. Inference optimizations achieve pose-to-ultrasound throughput of 81.2 FPS. To evaluate anatomical control beyond image similarity, we introduce the Action-Following Index (AFI), which measures normalized reconstruction gain over a static-prefix baseline. On 40 held-out 3D volumes, SonoAtlasWorld achieves liver and macro-organ AFI of 0.428 and 0.262, compared with at most 0.117 and 0.038 for the tested action- and geometry-conditioned methods. Long-rollout alignment reduces brightness drift by 3.46x at the end of 40 repeated scan cycles. SonoAtlasWorld also generates offline policy-training demonstrations and supports anatomically grounded closed-loop evaluation. Scaling the generated training data improves key-plane acquisition success from 48.2% to…

2611.26957.abs: This research examines how unsupported claims change as they move through multi-agent pipelines. It also examines whether preserving provenance can reduce these changes. We test both homogeneous and heterogeneous pipelines. Homogeneous pipelines use the same model across agents, while heterogeneous pipelines use different models. We compare the baseline with a provenance-aware framework. The framework passes each claim with its support status, source, evidence and transmission history. No new evidence is introduced during transmission. We measure changes in claim meaning, unsupported detail accretion, semantic drift, and provenance preservation. These metrics show whether the framework limits unsupported changes as claims pass between agents.

2611.26865.abs: Imitation learning for surgical robots is limited by the cost of collecting demonstrations. Meanwhile, many robot-assisted procedures are recorded as stereo video, yet policies cannot learn from them directly; clinical video carries no action labels. We present FlowScope, which pretrains a surgical policy network on unlabeled clinical video by forecasting scene flow, the metric 3D motion of scene points, with labels computed by off-the-shelf stereo depth and optical flow models. We pretrain the trunk of an Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) on a dataset of 1,149 clinical procedures (1.35M clips) and discard the flow head afterward, so the deployed policy is a standard ACT with no added inference cost. On a real surgical robotic system, FlowScope raises needle pickup success from 54% to 90% and first-handover success on needle regrasp from 4% to 52% (full task: 2% to 14%) over training from scratch (n=50 trials each), and retains its gains with a generative flow-matching action head. Ablations indicate that metric 3D motion is the strongest pretraining signal among those tested; kinematics, 2D tracks, depth alone, and scale-free 3D flow, each paired with kinematics, yield smaller or no gains. Representation analyses suggest that scene-flow pretraining encodes metric needle depth more accurately, that kinematics pretraining increases reliance on the robot state, and that needle-depth probes follow the ordering of real-robot success where offline validation error does not.

2611.26711.abs: Causal Abstraction defines a notion of \emph{equivalence} between a neural network and an algorithm, thus serving as a powerful framework for mechanistic interpretability. In this paper, however, we show the existence of a class of \emph{spurious features} which straightforwardly pass such equivalence tests. Suppose there are two directions in a model's representation space where: (i) one discriminates the input based on some feature, and (ii) the other steers the model towards a certain output. Interpretability methods based on Causal Abstraction (e.g., Distributed Alignment Search) can \emph{spuriously} simulate these directions' combined behavior by leveraging pathways passing through them, giving the impression that the model implements this feature. In such cases, we say the method discovered a \defn{parasite feature}. Experimentally, we show that Distributed Alignment Search finds parasite features using linear alignment maps in two tasks: syntactic agreement and two-digit addition. Our paper highlights an important consideration for Causal Abstraction and contributes to the ongoing debate about best practices for mechanistic interpretability.

ov.problema: La Causal Abstraction verifica se una rete neurale è equivalente a un algoritmo, ed è usata nell'interpretabilità meccanicistica. Gli autori mostrano che esistono 'feature parassite' che superano questi test di equivalenza senza che il modello implementi davvero la feature.
ov.idea: Se nello spazio delle rappresentazioni ci sono due direzioni — una che distingue l'input in base a una feature e una che spinge il modello verso un certo output — i metodi basati su Causal Abstraction (come Distributed Alignment Search) possono simulare il loro comportamento combinato passando attraverso queste direzioni, dando l'impressione che il modello implementi la feature. In questi casi si parla di 'parasite feature'.
ov.risultati: Sperimentalmente, Distributed Alignment Search trova feature parassite usando mappe di allineamento lineari in due compiti: accordo sintattico e addizione a due cifre.
ov.limiti: Il testo mostra il fenomeno solo su due compiti e con mappe lineari; resta un avvertimento sulle buone pratiche dell'interpretabilità, non una soluzione.

glossario.d: Framework che verifica se una rete è equivalente a un algoritmo astratto
Metodo che cerca direzioni nello spazio delle rappresentazioni per testare ipotesi
Feature apparente trovata dai metodi ma non realmente implementata dal modello

2611.29897.abs: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention. To enable efficient inference, we further develop an execution scheme tailored to this architecture, combining CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and execution-flow simplification while preserving the canonical history update. Evaluations on retargeted HiPHI demonstrate accurate terminal control over rollouts of up to 39.52 s, while short-horizon comparisons on BONES Seed and retargeted HumanML3D show that the model also retains strong spatial control and text-motion matching. On an RTX 4090, the optimized execution reduces median complete-window latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms, achieving a median paired speedup of 6.138times while preserving identical outputs and committed states in the tested rollouts. Moreover, we conduct extensive real-world evaluation on…

ov.problema: La generazione di movimento a lungo termine e controllabile in tempo reale è difficile: i metodi autoregressivi con diffusione hanno cache di attenzione limitate e denoising ripetuto costoso.
ov.idea: Motion Mamba 2.0 usa un'architettura Mamba per root-body con attenzione locale, stati ricorrenti ripristinabili e persistent content memory (PCM) che trasforma la storia compressa in slot aggiornabili; un execution scheme con CUDA Graph replay e kernel fusi riduce l'overhead.
ov.risultati: Su HiPHI retargeted controlla accuratamente rollout fino a 39.52 s; su RTX 4090 la latenza mediana completa scende da 1685.35 a 276.14 ms, con speedup mediano di 6.138x e output identici.
ov.limiti: I confronti a breve termine sono su BONES Seed e HumanML3D retargeted, quindi la generalizzazione a scenari diversi non è pienamente dimostrata.

glossario.d: architettura a spazio di stato con costo lineare nella lunghezza della sequenza
tecnica che registra e riesegue un grafo di operazioni GPU riducendo l'overhead

2611.31201.abs: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3\% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points. It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Beyond performance, controlled interventions indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation. These results provide both a practical recipe for building strong frontier-model-as-policy harnesses and a clearer account of the capabilities that drive their performance.

ov.problema: I modelli multimodali frontier possono agire come policy in robotica, ma non sono chiari i principi di progettazione degli harness (infrastrutture) che li usano in loop chiuso.
ov.idea: Embo-Harness studia quattro componenti del loop robotico (prompting, pianificazione, esecuzione azioni, uso di tool) e distilla sei findings in una ricetta pratica che privilegia interfacce che sfruttano il ragionamento visivo e l'uso di tool nativi del modello.
ov.risultati: Su RoboLab-120 raggiunge l'83.3% di successo, superando il miglior baseline riportato di 26.2 punti percentuali; riesce in 15 su 20 prove zero-shot su quattro task di manipolazione reali.
ov.limiti: Gli interventi controllati indicano che il modello dipende più dalla stima spaziale del target che dalla generazione esplicita di giunti o traiettorie, ma i risultati sono su un set limitato di task.

glossario.d: infrastruttura che collega un modello a osservazioni, azioni e tool in un loop
il modello affronta task mai visti senza addestramento specifico

2611.26954.abs: Video foresight reasoning requires vision-language models to anticipate future events or next actions from currently observed videos. Existing methods fit future captions, rationales, or full visual states, but face two limitations. First, they rely on annotations or external large models for supervision, limiting scalability. We address this with an on-policy self-distillation framework that turns past-future video pairs into a natural self-supervised signal without extra annotations or LLM supervision. Second, they treat the whole future clip as equally valuable, although most of it is irrelevant context information. We address this by defining a foresight score, from which we obtain a contrastive privilege advantage that drives the model to learn the most valuable future information. Since the score is intractable, we optimize a tractable lower-bound surrogate that interpolates this advantage, computed between the true and a random reference future, with a teacher-student distillation advantage; together, they amplify decision-relevant content information and suppress irrelevant context information. We call the resulting framework Future-OPSD. On open-ended prediction and closed-ended planning, Future-OPSD improves base models by up to 14.2 and 15.9 points without compromising general video understanding. Code will be available at https://jingchensun.github.io/future-opsd/

ov.problema: I modelli visione-linguaggio devono prevedere eventi futuri da video, ma i metodi esistenti richiedono annotazioni o modelli esterni e trattano tutto il futuro come ugualmente importante.
ov.idea: Future-OPSD usa coppie passato-futuro come segnale self-supervised senza annotazioni; definisce un foresight score e un contrastive privilege advantage per concentrarsi sulle informazioni future rilevanti, ottimizzando un lower-bound surrogato.
ov.risultati: Su predizione aperta e pianificazione chiusa, Future-OPSD migliora i modelli base fino a 14.2 e 15.9 punti senza compromettere la comprensione video generale.
ov.limiti: Il metodo si basa su un lower-bound surrogato e non è chiaro quanto sia robusto su domini video molto diversi.

glossario.d: il modello genera i dati e impara da una versione teacher di se stesso
vantaggio che confronta il futuro vero con uno casuale per premiare le informazioni utili

2611.30013.abs: Animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions requires both structural inference and motion control, yet existing motion benchmarks mostly cover conventional human or animal skeletons with simple instructions. We introduce DivDynBench, which evaluates rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories, with instructions requiring multi-phase part coordination and explicit timing, angle, repetition, and trajectory constraints. With large language models, we systematically compare three common paradigms: specialized motion generation, video generation followed by motion recovery, and direct agent-driven generation. We analyze their control capabilities, cross-morphology adaptability, and generation costs. Guided by this comparison, we propose an Agentic Motion Framework in which an agent writes compact parametric skeleton and motion programs, and a deterministic executor performs rigging, kinematic solving, and geometric correction. Compact parameter control reduces generation overhead and improves rigging reliability and motion-control accuracy, providing practical guidance for deploying complex 3D motion generation.

ov.problema: Animare asset 3D arbitrari da istruzioni richiede sia inferenza strutturale sia controllo del movimento, ma i benchmark esistenti coprono soprattutto scheletri umani o animali convenzionali con istruzioni semplici.
ov.idea: Introducono DivDynBench, che valuta rigging e generazione di movimento su sei categorie morfologiche con istruzioni che richiedono coordinazione multi-fase e vincoli espliciti di timing, angolo, ripetizione e traiettoria. Confrontano tre paradigmi (generazione specializzata, video generation con recupero del movimento, generazione diretta guidata da agente) e propongono un Agentic Motion Framework in cui l'agente scrive programmi parametrici compatti di scheletro e movimento, eseguiti da un executor deterministico.
ov.risultati: Il controllo parametrico compatto riduce l'overhead di generazione e migliora affidabilità del rigging e accuratezza del controllo del movimento, fornendo indicazioni pratiche per il deployment.

glossario.d: Costruire lo scheletro di controllo che permette di animare un modello 3D.
Calcolo delle posizioni delle parti a partire dai parametri di movimento delle articolazioni.

2611.28202.abs: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Bench, 120 diverse browser games grouped by how they respond to inaction and playable in real time or with the clock paused. With GPT-6.1 Sol under the same budgets, AutoPILOT reaches 68.6% real-time success against 38.3% for VISTA, and on GameWorld it keeps 80.0% in real time while VISTA drops from 84.1% to 42.9%. Its gains hold across models, and it reaches VISTA's final success rate at a fifth of its API cost. Our results suggest that how a harness turns model outputs into actions over time is a central yet underexplored part of agent design, and we hope AutoPILOT and AFK-Bench will serve as a foundation for agents in a world that does not wait.

ov.problema: I modelli multimodali giocano bene ai videogiochi quando il gioco aspetta, ma falliscono quando il gioco continua in tempo reale. Gran parte del divario sta nell'harness (l'infrastruttura che decide cosa vede il modello e come i suoi output diventano azioni).
ov.idea: AutoPILOT cambia il modo in cui gli output diventano azioni: in ogni chiamata il modello può inviare un'azione primitiva, avviare una macro ad anello aperto o scrivere un controllore ad anello chiuso che continua a giocare dallo schermo senza nuove chiamate al modello. Costruiscono anche AFK-Bench, 120 giochi browser in tempo reale.
ov.risultati: Con GPT-6.1 Sol e gli stessi budget, AutoPILOT raggiunge il 68,6% di successo in tempo reale contro il 38,3% di VISTA; su GameWorld mantiene l'80,0% in tempo reale mentre VISTA scende dall'84,1% al 42,9%. Raggiunge il successo finale di VISTA a un quinto del costo API.
ov.limiti: I risultati dipendono da modelli specifici e da un nuovo benchmark; il testo non chiarisce quanto si generalizzi a giochi non browser o ad altri harness.

glossario.d: Infrastruttura che gestisce input, memoria e azioni di un agente attorno al modello.
Sequenza di azioni predefinita eseguita senza controllare lo schermo nel frattempo.
Codice che osserva lo schermo e decide azioni senza nuove chiamate al modello.

2611.30989.abs: AI systems can now operate Blender, follow instructions in complex video games, and manipulate objects with robot arms. What range of physical goals can today's AI systems achieve autonomously? Answering this question requires testing systems on tasks that demand different combinations of perception, memory, planning, and action. We introduce WorldLeague, a benchmark that compares AI systems on a common set of 60 simulated robot tasks by measuring progress toward each task's physical goal from the robot's trajectory. Robots explore scenes to gather evidence in WorldSeek, rearrange objects in WorldShape, and adapt to changes in WorldShift. Tying these goals to a single control interface limits which AI systems can be compared. In WorldLeague, vision-language models (VLMs) choose targets and motions, while vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs) use their native controls. For each of six capability dimensions, we measure how much progress a system makes toward its goals (Interactive Score) and how often it achieves them (physical success rate). Together, these measures form the system's Physical Agency Profile. Among 13 representative AI systems, Claude Fable 5.2 achieves 13 of the 60 goals and earns the highest mean Interactive Score (28.58/100). Fable leads in four dimensions, while GPT-6.1-Sol and GPT-6-Astra tie for first on rule-following tasks. Even when VLMs answer every final question correctly, they receive an Interactive Score of zero in 71.8\% of those episodes. WorldLeague gives Embodied AI, Physical AI, and Agentic AI a shared basis…

ov.problema: Non è chiaro quale gamma di obiettivi fisici i sistemi AI attuali possano raggiungere autonomamente; serve un benchmark che testi combinazioni di percezione, memoria, pianificazione e azione.
ov.idea: WorldLeague confronta sistemi AI su 60 task robotici simulati misurando il progresso verso l'obiettivo fisico dalla traiettoria. I task sono in tre ambienti: WorldSeek (esplorazione), WorldShape (riordino oggetti), WorldShift (adattamento a cambiamenti). VLMs scelgono target e movimenti, mentre VLAs e WAMs usano i loro controlli nativi.
ov.risultati: Tra 13 sistemi, Claude Fable 5.2 raggiunge 13 dei 60 obiettivi e il miglior Interactive Score medio (28.58/100); guida in quattro dimensioni, mentre GPT-6.1-Sol e GPT-6-Astra pari-meritano sul rule-following. Anche quando i VLMs rispondono correttamente a tutte le domande finali, ricevono Interactive Score zero nel 71% dei casi.
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe sul dato 71%; il benchmark è in simulazione e legato a una singola interfaccia di controllo.

glossario.d: Vision-Language-Action model: modello che mappa visione e linguaggio in azioni robotiche.
World-Action Model: modello che usa una rappresentazione del mondo per pianificare azioni.
Misura del progresso verso l'obiettivo fisico lungo la traiettoria del robot.

2611.29338.abs: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions. Meanwhile, CP-SFT uses an explicit robot-specific system prompt to constrain manipulation outputs to a structured action space, aiming to focus adaptation on robot-specific contexts and promote specialization while minimizing interference with broader pretrained capabilities. With this formulation, we train nanoAstra on more than 5,000 hours of robot data together with general VQA data. On RoboTwin 2.0's randomized benchmark, nanoAstra-9B achieves a 17.8% zero-shot success rate, substantially outperforming advanced VLA and WAM baselines as well as similarly sized VLMs. With inference faster than the corresponding motion execution on a single H20 GPU, our model supports action-chunk-like streaming execution that overlaps inference with motion, reducing the robot's idle time from 35.0% to 6.9%.

ov.problema: GPT-6 Astra mostra forte generalizzazione nel controllo robotico, ma la scarsa divulgazione del training rende difficile riprodurre tali capacità.
ov.idea: nanoAstra addestra VLMs per manipolazione generalizzabile combinando semantic action modeling (comportamenti come passi semantici fatti di primitive d'azione riutilizzabili e parametrizzate, guidate da descrizioni di progresso) e CP-SFT (supervised fine-tuning che preserva le capacità), che usa un system prompt robot-specifico per vincolare gli output a uno spazio d'azione strutturato, specializzando senza interferire con le capacità pre-addestrate.
ov.risultati: Addestrato su oltre 5.000 ore di dati robotici più VQA generale, nanoAstra-9B raggiunge il 17.8% di success rate zero-shot su RoboTwin 2.0, superando baseline VLA e WAM avanzate e VLMs di dimensioni simili. L'inferenza è più veloce dell'esecuzione del movimento su una singola GPU H20, permettendo streaming con azioni a chunk e riducendo il tempo di inattività del robot dal 35.0% al 6.9%.
ov.limiti: Il success rate zero-shot resta basso (17.8%); i risultati sono su un singolo benchmark simulato.

glossario.d: Supervised fine-tuning che preserva le capacità: adatta il modello senza degradare quelle generali.
Azioni robotiche di base riutilizzabili e parametrizzabili.
Blocco di più azioni eseguite insieme per ridurre i tempi morti.

2611.30662.abs: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five open-source) covering eight business scenarios and complement it with 64 public general-purpose benchmarks. On the e-commerce suite, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B surpasses substantially larger open-source flagship models, including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, HY4, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. On the general-purpose suite, every WeMM-Ecom model surpasses its similarly sized Qwen3.5 counterpart, with the lightweight variants (e.g., WeMM-Ecom-2B) showing clear advantages over leading lightweight models such as Qwen3.5-2B, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B, and LFM3-VL-2B. Beyond benchmarks, WeMM-Ecom now powers hundreds of production use cases in WeChat, including catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce, serving billion-scale requests per day. We publicly release all model weights and detail our data curation, training recipe, and benchmark construction to…

2611.31115.abs: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions. To systematically study its impact, we introduce RUIBench, comprising 30 manipulation tasks across five suites spanning world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, and contact-rich manipulation. We further develop RUIKit, a unified framework that crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms, yielding 13 interfaces under shared perception and control. In simulation, changing only the RUI shifts a frontier agent's success rate from 45% to 81%, and that of a fine-tuned 4B model from 13% to 47%. Our analysis reveals that effective interfaces reduce unnecessary decisions while preserving essential feedback, with their benefits shaped by agent behavior and physical uncertainty. We further uncover a verification gap, where agents frequently declare success despite observable failures, revealing the need for task-level verification beyond individual actions. Together, these findings establish RUI design as a critical factor in embodied agent reliability.

ov.problema: I foundation model sanno ragionare su compiti fisici, ma tradurre questa intelligenza in esecuzione robotica affidabile è difficile; un fattore trascurato è l'interfaccia robot-use (RUI), cioè come gli agenti esprimono ed eseguono azioni fisiche.
ov.idea: Gli autori introducono RUIBench, 30 task di manipolazione in 5 suite (world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, contact-rich manipulation), e RUIKit, un framework che incrocia 6 astrazioni d'azione con 2 forme di interazione, ottenendo 13 interfacce sotto percezione e controllo condivisi.
ov.risultati: In simulazione, cambiare solo la RUI fa passare il success rate di un agente frontier dal 45% all'81%, e di un modello 4B fine-tuned dal 13% al 47%. Emerge un verification gap: gli agenti dichiarano spesso successo nonostante fallimenti osservabili.
ov.limiti: Studio in simulazione; i risultati dipendono dal comportamento dell'agente e dall'incertezza fisica.

glossario.d: Robot-use interface: modo in cui un agente esprime ed esegue azioni fisiche su un robot.
Divario tra il successo dichiarato dall'agente e il successo realmente osservato.

2611.30157.abs: Effective real-time, full-duplex multimodal interaction requires systems to understand not only what users say, but also the communicative needs conveyed through prosody, facial expressions, gestures, and context, and to generate audiovisual responses that appropriately address those needs. Existing evaluations offer limited insight into whether systems translate an understanding of such unspoken needs into effective responses. We introduce UUBench, a benchmark for assessing how well multimodal interactive systems Understand the Unspoken intent and address users' implicit communicative needs. The inherent subjectivity of implicit intent inference poses a key challenge for evaluation. To address this, we introduce Process-Oriented Scoring, which grounds the assessment of intent fulfillment in observable auditory and visual cues, such as prosody and gestures. Rather than relying solely on a single overall score, it evaluates how well a response addresses the communicative needs conveyed by each applicable primitive dimension. We aggregate the dimension-level scores according to each dimension's relevance to the annotated evidence. Beyond intent fulfillment, Outcome-Oriented Scoring evaluates the naturalness, appropriateness, and human-likeness of the reply itself under audio-only, visual-only, and audiovisual conditions. To make these judgments traceable to observable evidence, we propose a Fact-Grounded Scoring JEV module, which uses structured, timestamped audiovisual observations of the user and the digital human's reply to assess one dimension or criterion at a time.…

2611.29355.abs: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. We introduce Polytropos, a benchmark that measures what model descriptions of cultural objects keep of the particular object by turning each description back into an image and comparing it with the original photograph. On 374 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty, with 1,870 descriptions from five models and 230 written by curators, reconstructions are recognised as the recorded culture more often than the photographs, at 54.55% to 59.09% against 52.14%, yet 16% to 21% of objects change outcome and only 0.49% of reconstructions are identified as the specific object. On the same objects, models lose recorded cultures at a rate similar to curators but gain more. Model descriptions give each object many faces, each typical of its culture and almost none the object itself.

2611.29238.abs: AI-driven game development holds the potential to transform diverse human inspirations into interactive experiences. However, existing systems and benchmarks primarily focus on explicit development specifications, with limited support for adapting multimodal references and evaluating actual gameplay experiences. We introduce GameAnything, an open-source agentic platform that transforms multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games through iterative development. GameAnything integrates coding agents with an independent playtesting critic, persistent development state, and reusable experience memory to support continuous refinement. We further present GameAnything-Bench, a benchmark spanning diverse reference modalities, game creation objectives, and gaming environments, with exploratory gameplay testing to assess both functional correctness and gameplay quality. Evaluations of nine coding agent configurations reveal that current agents can adapt reference content but still struggle with playable interactions and precise modifications. Moreover, multimodal references improve content fidelity, while iterative refinement yields substantial but varying improvements across agents. These findings highlight both the potential and remaining challenges of inspiration-driven game development.

2611.27376.abs: RL post-training typically produces domain experts that must then be consolidated into one model, and as new experts keep arriving, this consolidation becomes a continual process. Weight merging and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) must re-consolidate the whole model whenever an expert is added, and can erode capabilities outside the target domains. We propose Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation (CSPD), which keeps the pre-RL model frozen, distills each RL expert independently into a soft prompt, and composes experts by concatenating their prompts without joint training. A single soft prompt suffices to distill an RL expert, recovering at least 90% of the teacher's gain in 22 of 23 math, code, and agent settings. Independently trained prompts compose well. In a multi-expert setting, the average rises with every expert added, and the full composition matches MOPD (67.83 vs. 67.79). The composition generalizes best across six held-out benchmarks. Input-space adaptation adds little serving overhead, keeping throughput within 1.5% of the unadapted backbone and reaching 2.40x that of rank-4 LoRA. These results point toward continual post-training on a fixed backbone.

ov.problema: Dopo il post-training con RL si ottengono esperti di dominio che vanno consolidati in un unico modello; aggiungere nuovi esperti richiede di ri-consolidare tutto e può erodere capacità fuori dai domini target.
ov.idea: CSPD mantiene il modello pre-RL congelato, distilla ogni esperto RL in un soft prompt separato e compone gli esperti concatenando i prompt senza training congiunto.
ov.risultati: Un singolo soft prompt recupera almeno il 90% del guadagno del teacher in 22 su 23 setting di matematica, codice e agenti; la composizione completa eguaglia MOPD (67.83 vs 67.79) e generalizza meglio su sei benchmark; throughput entro l'1.5% del backbone non adattato e 2.40x rispetto a LoRA rank-4.
ov.limiti: I risultati si basano su 23 setting specifici e non è chiaro se la composizione regga con molti esperti o domini molto diversi.

glossario.d: vettori di input appresi che condizionano il modello senza modificarne i pesi
trasferire il comportamento di un modello teacher a uno studente più piccolo o a un prompt
multi-teacher on-policy distillation: distillazione da più teacher con dati generati dallo studente

2611.28618.abs: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories. Across Navigation, Sokoban, and spatial mapping, even one online training task supports transfer to other tasks. Four fixed trajectories raise a 4B student's success from 49.17% to 82.08% on standard Navigation and from 60.16% to 85.55% on Sokoban, recovering over 90% of the measured gap to a 27B teacher on these panels. On an independent Navigation panel, replay improves success from 45.83% to 76.67%, retaining 91.36% of the same-task online gain without new interaction during optimization. Training repetitions, matched supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and a 9B extension further support the value of compact experience.

ov.problema: Addestrare un agente visivo capace richiede molte interazioni registrate, che sono costose da raccogliere. Il paper studia quanta poca esperienza di interazione basti per distillare (trasferire) le capacità di un insegnante più grande in uno studente più piccolo.
ov.idea: Selezionano poche traiettorie rappresentative usando la copertura di abilità e contesto e la somiglianza delle decisioni visive ordinate. Poi usano la distillazione on-policy (OPD): lo studente impara interagendo di nuovo sulle traiettorie scelte o rispondendo di nuovo a storie fisse.
ov.risultati: Quattro traiettorie fisse portano il successo di uno studente 4B dal 49,17% all'82,08% su Navigation e dal 60,16% all'85,55% su Sokoban, recuperando oltre il 90% del divario misurato verso un insegnante 27B. Su un pannello Navigation indipendente il replay migliora il successo dal 45,83% al 76,67%.
ov.limiti: I risultati sono misurati su pochi ambienti (Navigation, Sokoban, mappatura spaziale) e con un insegnante specifico; non è chiaro quanto si generalizzi ad altri domini.

glossario.d: Lo studente impara dalle proprie nuove interazioni, non solo imitando traiettorie fisse dell'insegnante.
Sequenza registrata di osservazioni e azioni di un agente durante un compito.

2611.28833.abs: Frontier language models can now read and edit the weights of a neural network much like code and thereby improve a small model, an approach known as Weight-Space Programming (WSP). We further explore applying WSP to a language model itself, which we call Self-WSP. Specifically, Qwen3.5-0.8B reads its own weights, proposes an edit, and then continues with the edited weights as both problem solver and editor. We find many cases of genuine self-improvement. Self-edits can raise GSM8K accuracy from 11.8% to 62.2% and MATH500 accuracy from 7.0% to 32.2%, sometimes by changing only 16 parameters, and in some cases repeated self-editing keeps improving the model. A closer look, however, reveals that these gains lack interpretability. The model shows little understanding of the edits it makes, and WSP driven by random search sometimes performs comparably. Self-WSP thus holds promise as a path toward recursive self-improvement (RSI), but realizing this promise requires further exploration.

ov.problema: I modelli frontier possono leggere e modificare i pesi di una rete come codice (Weight-Space Programming), ma non è chiaro se un modello possa migliorare se stesso in questo modo.
ov.idea: Self-WSP fa leggere a Qwen3.5-0.8B i propri pesi, proporre una modifica e continuare con i pesi modificati sia come risolutore che come editor.
ov.risultati: Le auto-modifiche alzano l'accuratezza su GSM8K dall'11.8% al 62.2% e su MATH500 dal 7.0% al 32.2%, a volte cambiando solo 16 parametri; in alcuni casi auto-modifiche ripetute continuano a migliorare il modello.
ov.limiti: I guadagni mancano di interpretabilità: il modello mostra poca comprensione delle modifiche e la ricerca casuale nei pesi a volte performa in modo comparabile.

glossario.d: modificare i pesi di una rete neurale come se fossero codice
un modello che migliora se stesso in modo iterativo

2611.25476.abs: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. Once installed, the new capabilities run independently of the language model. Given a grammar or eight demonstrations, weight programs enable previously unseen command compositions (0% to 99.8% exact match) and a new pickup action (0% to 98.4% success), while preserving the original command and navigation capabilities. On ImageNet, four weight programs achieve net gains of 8.84-17.62 points while preserving clean accuracy, outperforming the best of eight fine-tuning methods under matched examples, checks, and retention constraints. In a Vision Transformer, causal interventions show that installed noise-correction gates drive robustness gains, while their selective activation preserves clean accuracy. Rerun on five independently trained Vision Transformers without further language model calls, ten weight programs retain 83-110% of their source-network gains on average, whereas copying their fixed weight edits yields negligible gains. Six programs written for an already edited network add…

ov.problema: Aggiungere nuove capacità a una rete neurale di solito richiede addestramento con gradienti, che è costoso e può degradare le capacità già apprese. Il paper vuole installare nuove abilità direttamente nei pesi di una rete già addestrata.
ov.idea: Weight-Space Programming (WSP): un linguaggio congelato scrive programmi eseguibili che leggono, costruiscono o modificano direttamente i pesi della rete, usando conoscenza del compito e i pesi esistenti. Una volta installate, le nuove capacità funzionano senza il linguaggio.
ov.risultati: Con una grammatica o otto dimostrazioni, i programmi di pesi portano composizioni di comandi mai viste dallo 0% al 99,8% di corrispondenza esatta e una nuova azione di raccolta dallo 0% al 98,4% di successo, preservando le capacità originali. Su ImageNet quattro programmi danno guadagni netti di 8,84-17,62 punti superando il migliore di otto metodi di fine-tuning.
ov.limiti: Il testo è troncato e non chiarisce i costi o i requisiti per scrivere i programmi; i risultati su ImageNet dipendono da esempi e vincoli di conservazione specifici.

glossario.d: Scrivere programmi che modificano direttamente i pesi di una rete, senza addestramento con gradienti.
Modificare una parte della rete per verificare se è quella a causare un comportamento.

2611.30813.abs: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.

ov.problema: Il vision pretrained è un punto di partenza comune per il robot learning, ma i confronti misurano di solito un solo vettore pooled da un'immagine in terza persona, mentre le policy bimanuali leggono token densi per patch da telecamere sul robot.
ov.idea: Introducono HIVE-Bench: una policy flow-matching condivisa legge 20 encoder di sette famiglie su 24 task bimanuali egocentrici, in adattamento, condivisione dei task e sweep di dati, dimensione del modello e layer. I token per patch vengono poi valutati con statistiche, readout di stato e oggetti, punteggi vision pubblicati e un readout di dinamica inversa.
